top_stories.title: 18 insights from SailPoint’s Navigate event: Enterprises race to bring identity security for AI agents up to machine speed
top_stories.summary: SailPoint's Navigate event surfaced 18 key insights on enterprise identity security for AI agents, highlighting how AI agents are acquiring unintended access at scale and creating new challenges for identity governance. The discussion centered on the need for machine-speed identity controls as AI agent populations grow into the thousands within organizations.

top_stories.title: Tenable Identity Exposure SaaS Has CVSS 9.9 Command Injection That Hands Attackers SYSTEM on the Domain Controller
top_stories.summary: A critical command injection vulnerability (CVE-2026-106126) with a CVSS score of 9.9 has been disclosed in Tenable Identity Exposure, a SaaS-based Active Directory security and identity threat detection platform. The flaw allows attackers to execute commands that grant SYSTEM-level access on the domain controller.

top_stories.title: How to keep AI agents within their permissions
top_stories.summary: The article addresses the challenge of AI agents operating beyond their assigned permissions using valid credentials, a gap in traditional access control models. Token Security outlines approaches for enforcing agent-specific authorization policies while maintaining operational autonomy.

top_stories.title: The Third-Party Agent Problem: Why Security Built for AI You Chose Misses the Agents You Didn't
top_stories.summary: A report on agent security reveals that in studied environments, approximately 1,280 third-party products embed AI agents, but only 282 authenticate through SSO, leaving roughly 1,000 invisible to identity infrastructure. The article addresses the governance gap created when AI agents bypass standard authentication flows, framing it as a structural challenge for identity and access management programs.

top_stories.title: The AI Velocity Paradox: Why Security Is Decades Behind AI Ambition
top_stories.summary: SailPoint's "Horizons of Identity Security" report identifies a "velocity paradox" where enterprises deploy autonomous AI agents while relying on legacy, human-speed identity security architectures. The report highlights the gap between AI-driven business operations and outdated security controls as a critical challenge for identity security programs.

news.title: Credential-Stealing GitHub Actions Workflows Planted in Tens of Thousands of Repositories
news.summary: A credential-theft campaign has compromised two high-profile open-source maintainer accounts to inject malicious GitHub Actions workflows into over 340 repositories. The attacker used the compromised account of pyxel author Takashi Kitao to push malicious workflows to 27 repositories, with the campaign focused on stealing credentials from CI/CD pipelines.

news.title: Citrix Patches Critical NetScaler Flaw That Could Enable RCE in SAML Deployments
news.summary: Citrix has released patches for a critical memory overflow vulnerability (CVE-2026-107406) in NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway that can enable remote code execution or denial-of-service. The flaw specifically affects SAML deployments, making it directly relevant to IAM professionals managing federated authentication infrastructure.

news.title: FBI Says China-Linked Hackers Ran Portal Giving Third Parties Access to Stolen Emails
news.summary: The FBI and agencies from six countries reported that hackers linked to Chinese cybersecurity firm Integrity Technology Group stole emails from government, law enforcement, healthcare, and religious organizations in Southeast Asia. The hackers operated a portal allowing third-party access to stolen email data, with Integrity Technology Group subsequently sanctioned by the U.S. and UK.

news.title: ‘The gap was not the awareness’: The company phishing trainings you loathe aren’t enough when nearly 1 in 4 security pros say their MFA is optional
news.summary: A survey found that nearly 1 in 4 security professionals report that MFA is optional at their organizations, despite 44% indicating an AI-driven phishing attack successfully penetrated their defenses last year. The findings highlight a gap between perceived security posture and actual MFA enforcement practices among security teams.

news.title: U.S. Offers Up to $10 Million for Tips on Zhang Yu, Charged in HAFNIUM Hacks
news.summary: The U.S. State Department is offering up to $10 million for information on Zhang Yu, a Chinese national charged in connection with the 2021 HAFNIUM Microsoft Exchange Server attacks. The HAFNIUM campaign exploited critical vulnerabilities in Microsoft Exchange Server to gain unauthorized access to email accounts and networks across thousands of organizations.

news.title: ID Dataweb Named "Overall ID Management Solution of the Year" in the 2026 CyberSecurity Breakthrough Awards Program
news.summary: ID Dataweb was named "Overall ID Management Solution of the Year" in the 2026 CyberSecurity Breakthrough Awards Program. The company specializes in identity threat detection and risk mitigation for enterprises.

news.title: Anugal Announces U.S. SAP IDM Readiness Campaign Ahead of 2027 Maintenance Deadline
news.summary: Anugal, a product of Business Core Solutions, has launched a U.S. campaign to help enterprises prepare for the SAP Identity Management (SAP IDM) end-of-maintenance deadline in 2027. The campaign focuses on uncovering hidden SAP IDM dependencies, maintaining governance continuity, and reducing migration risk as organizations transition away from the platform.

news.title: The people who know passkeys best are still typing passwords
news.summary: A Yubico and Okta survey of 1,890 technology and security professionals across nine countries found that 43% still use username and password as their primary work account sign-in method, despite 87% reporting familiarity with passkeys. The data highlights a gap between passkey awareness and adoption among the very professionals expected to champion modern authentication methods.

news.title: SonicWall Patches CVSS 10.0 Pre-Authentication SSRF Flaw in SMA1000 Appliances
news.summary: SonicWall has released hotfixes addressing four vulnerabilities in its SMA1000 appliances, including a CVSS 10.0 pre-authentication SSRF flaw. The critical flaw allows unauthenticated attackers to send requests through the appliance to reach internal network functions, affecting remote access gateway infrastructure.

news.title: Browser-in-browser attacks use fake Meta Muse Ad lure to steal credentials
news.summary: A browser-in-browser (BitB) phishing campaign is using fake Meta Muse advertisements to steal user credentials through convincing fake login pages. The attack technique renders a simulated browser window within the real browser to spoof legitimate authentication pages, bypassing user awareness of phishing URLs.

news.title: Kiteworks & Citrix Incidents Show Challenges of Zero-Day Response
news.summary: Kiteworks and Citrix both faced zero-day vulnerability incidents, with Kiteworks instructing customers to power down its data-protection platform during a nine-hour window while Citrix stayed silent on reported attacks before releasing a patch. The incidents highlight differing vendor response approaches to zero-day disclosures, a key concern for IAM and access management professionals given Citrix's role in secure remote access infrastructure.

news.title: SWIFT Banking & Government Middleware Enables RCE
news.summary: A vulnerability in SWIFT banking and government middleware enables remote code execution (RCE). The flaw can be exploited to bypass hardware-based MFA in high-security environments, with patching recommended as the immediate mitigation.

news.title: Microsoft Plugs Nearly 1,000 Security Holes
news.summary: Microsoft released a record-breaking patch batch addressing at least 974 security vulnerabilities across Windows and other software. AI is being credited for accelerating vulnerability discovery, though security experts note organizations are struggling to keep pace with testing and deploying the volume of monthly fixes.

news.title: FBI Probes Service Selling 153M+ Drivers Licenses
news.summary: A dark web service is selling digital scans of over 153 million U.S. and Canadian driver's licenses, with images apparently sourced from a Louisiana-based identity verification company. The FBI's New Orleans field office has opened an official inquiry into the breach.
